needs: Distinguish population and sample; judge generalisation

skill.title: Interpret a histogram in terms of distribution
Interpret an analysis and relate it to the original question
skill.example: 60% prefer A → answer the survey question
needs: Recognise how sampling variability affects conclusions

lines.text: The null hypothesis says nothing has changed from 65%.
65% lies inside the 95% interval, so there is not enough evidence to reject $H_0$.
Conclusion: at the 5% level of significance, the Netflix share of the market has not changed.

references.final: \text{Fail to reject } H_0: \text{ the Netflix share has not changed}

lines.text: The null hypothesis $H_0$: the mean spend is $\text{€}94$ (the supermarket is right).
The alternative hypothesis $H_1$: the mean spend is not $\text{€}94$.
At the 5% level (two-tailed) the critical values are $\pm 1.96$.
$z$ lies between $-1.96$ and $1.96$, so we do not reject $H_0$. There is not enough evidence to reject $H_0$ (the claim of $\text{€}94$).

references.final: \text{Do not reject } H_0\ (z = -1.71).\ \text{There is not enough evidence to reject } H_0 \text{ (the claim of } \text{€}94\text{).}

lines.text: The population mean was $\text{€}39\,400$. We test whether it has changed (either direction), so the test is two-tailed.
At the $5\%$ level, two-tailed, the critical values are $\pm 1.96$.
$z$ lies outside $[-1.96, 1.96]$, so the result is significant. Reject $H_0$.
There is evidence that the mean annual income of full-time workers has changed since the national data were published.

references.final: z = -2.74 < -1.96\text{, so reject } H_0\text{: the mean income has changed}
